clue.text: Jumped-up bureaucrat to chuck up job

parts.note: to chuck something up is to abandon it, in British slang to jack it in
an office is a post or position, as in holding high office

explanation.surface: A self-important civil servant decides to quit his post.
explanation.walkthrough: The link word 'to' joins definition and wordplay. To 'jack in' is British slang for giving something up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old idiom for a petty official who throws his weight about.

clue.text: Only a sweet, right?

parts.note: only and just are synonyms, as in it is only a scratch
an ice is an ice cream, a sweet course or treat

explanation.surface: Someone checks that what they are being offered is merely a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right?' looks like a tag question; it is the noun, what is fair and lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Right, as a noun, is a synonym for fairness and lawfulness, as in fighting for right.

clue.text: Warm drink

definitions.meaning: friendly and hearty, as in a warm welcome
a sweet fruit squash or a liqueur

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means friendly and heartfelt; as a noun it is a sweet fruit beverage or liqueur.

clue.text: Rough, in a gentle fashion

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape or mould it, so the letters before it are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone manages to be coarse while seeming mild-mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' reads as the noun meaning manner, but as a verb it tells you to remould IN A GENTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rough is unpolished and lacking in grace or refinement.

clue.text: It follows old trains up the track

indicators.note: follows tells you that this piece comes after the others
in a down clue, up means the letters are written from bottom to top

parts.note: BR was British Rail, the former national train operator in Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something trails vintage locomotives along the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail ran Britain's trains until the 1990s, hence the abbreviation. 'up' works because this is a down entry, and 'follows' sends the first word of the clue to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The path a planet or satellite travels round is its track through space.

clue.text: Weird arrangement of sails incorporated in vessel

indicators.note: incorporated in means one piece is taken into the body of the other

parts.note: weird is an old noun for destiny, as in the Weird Sisters
a ship's rig is the way its masts and sails are set out

explanation.surface: A ship is fitted with a strange configuration of canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird' looks like an adjective describing the arrangement; it is the old noun meaning destiny, as in Macbeth's Weird Sisters, and 'incorporated in' makes it the container.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a type of warship, so an example of a ship.

clue.text: Sword injured a girl

parts.note: cut, as a past tense, means wounded
lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a young woman

explanation.surface: A blade has wounded a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a short curved blade once carried by sailors, so a kind of weapon.

clue.text: One on the fiddle may be excessively obsequious

definitions.meaning: a violinist may draw the stick across the strings and, if unskilled, make a grating noise
to behave in a fawning, servile way

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to grovel, and whimsically describes what a violinist does to the strings.

clue.text: American man about to pass comment

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the short word before it is read backwards

parts.note: bo is American slang for a fellow, used as a form of address
to serve time is to pass it, as a prisoner does

explanation.surface: A man from the States is on the point of making a remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' alone turns BO into OB, and 'to pass' gives SERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark on something is a synonym: both mean to say what you have noticed.

clue.text: Verbally attack an irritating person

definitions.meaning: to scold fiercely, as in a scorching criticism
old slang for an annoying individual

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to scold scorchingly; as dated slang it is a tiresome nuisance of a human.

clue.text: Revival of sin turning up in various countries

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the rearranged letters
various suggests different forms, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
in a down clue, turning up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to err is to do wrong, to sin

explanation.surface: Wickedness is making a comeback in several nations.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests vice spreading through several nations. 'various' is the anagram signal, not a count, and 'turning up in' both inverts the word for sin and tucks it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a return to life or use after seeming dead.

clue.text: I'm foolish when I take a number

indicators.note: take means the pieces before it have the next piece added on

parts.note: as means when, as in she arrived as I left
nine is one example of a number

explanation.surface: Someone admits they act stupidly whenever they pick a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm' only links the definition to the wordplay; the letter the answer needs comes from the second 'I', and 'take' simply adds on the number.
explanation.definitionFit: It literally means like a donkey, so stupid or silly.

clue.text: Peg said "I lay claim to brewers' preparations"

indicators.note: said tells you the word before it is spoken, giving a different spelling with the same pronunciation

parts.note: a tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on
bags is what British children shout to claim something, as in bags I go first

explanation.surface: A woman called Peg announces that she owns the beer-makers' mixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' or 'bags I' is British playground slang for claiming first right to something. The brewers are people making a pot of tea, not beer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the little sachets of leaves made ready for anyone brewing a cuppa.

clue.text: Live broadcast loses all exterior sound

indicators.note: losing all the exterior strips away every letter outside the very centre of the word

parts.note: to radio a message is to broadcast it
sound means healthy or well, as in sound in body

explanation.surface: A programme going out in real time has its outdoor audio cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' reads as the adjective for a real-time programme; it is the verb. 'loses all exterior' strips RADIO to its central D.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is a synonym, as in to live in a cottage.

clue.text: Someone attacking the king in time replaced Lawrence

indicators.note: in places the royal cipher inside the word for a period

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
GR is Georgius Rex, the cipher of the British kings named George

indicators.note: replaced, read as put back, means the name is written backwards

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, enlisted in the RAF under the name Ross

explanation.surface: An assailant of the monarch eventually took over from a man named Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross was the alias T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, used when he joined the RAF. 'replaced' must be read as 'put back', a reversal, and 'in' as an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who starts hostilities or makes the first assault.

clue.text: People attending the game fail to gain admission without paying

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators at a sports match
to crash is to fail suddenly, as a business or computer does

explanation.surface: Football fans do not manage to sneak in free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fail to gain admission' reads as one phrase, but 'fail' alone is wordplay and the definition starts at 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: It means to enter a party or event uninvited or with no ticket.

clue.text: Change of government due to pact being broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters before it are put together differently

explanation.surface: A new administration comes in because an agreement has been violated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due to' reads as 'because of', but it is part of the letters that 'being broken' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden, often violent seizure of power that replaces those ruling a state.

clue.text: Accepted ten pound note in advance for a tool

indicators.note: in advance means the note goes ahead of the pound rather than after it

parts.note: U means upper-class and so socially acceptable, from the British U and non-U distinction
taken as written
si is a note of the sol-fa scale, another name for ti
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone took a tenner up front as payment for an implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in advance' tells you the note SI goes before the pound L, though the clue names the pound first. U is British shorthand for upper-class, hence acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement, especially one used in the kitchen.

clue.text: Red plot disrupted globe on a very small scale

definitions.text: globe on a very small scale

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A communist conspiracy upset a tiny model of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny bead of liquid is a minute sphere.

clue.text: Part of the job a steersman does, to tack

indicators.note: part of means the answer is a stretch of consecutive letters inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Changing a boat's course against the wind is one of the helmsman's duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tack' reads as sailing a zigzag course, fitting the steersman; here it is the sewing sense, stitching loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: In sewing, both mean to stitch fabric loosely and temporarily.

clue.text: Thief has difficulty climbing — 'e's out of the light

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: the rub is the snag or difficulty, as in there's the rub

indicators.note: out of means the named letter is taken away from the word that follows

parts.note: a glare is a harsh, dazzling light
the dropped-aitch 'e stands for the letter E

explanation.surface: A robber struggles to scale a wall, staying hidden in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns RUB into BUR, and 'out of' removes E from GLARE to leave GLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks into buildings to steal.

clue.text: Second horse, we hear, lapped by crossbreed in run

indicators.note: to lap is to wrap round, so the crossbreed's letters enclose the horse's

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a donkey and a horse

indicators.note: we hear tells you the child's word for a horse is given by its pronunciation, written as two letters

parts.note: gee-gee is a British child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: The runner-up in a race is overtaken by a mongrel animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like the race; it means running contraband. 'we hear' takes a British child's word for a horse by its pronunciation, and 'lapped by' means wrapped inside, not overtaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To run guns or drugs is to carry them illegally across a border.

clue.text: A number of people around lunch time blossom

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for the people is read backwards

parts.note: men are a group of people
one o'clock is a usual hour for lunch

explanation.surface: Several folk bloom at about midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blossom' reads as a verb, what the people do at midday, but it is the noun; 'around' is a reversal here, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a flowering plant, so an example of a bloom.

clue.text: With others only jeering, I bet I pick the winners

indicators.note: only the others means you keep every second letter of the words that follow and drop the rest

explanation.surface: A lone tipster, mocked by everyone else, insists he can choose the winning horses.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that draws the winning numbers for Britain's Premium Bonds, a government savings lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the British Premium Bonds computer, which selects the prize-winning bond numbers each month.

clue.text: It's dishonest to sound happy about being confined to bed

indicators.note: being confined to means the turned word is shut inside the word for a bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the contented noise is read backwards

parts.note: a cat purrs when it is content

explanation.surface: Pretending to be cheerful about being laid up ill is a kind of lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' links to the definition. 'about' does not mean concerning: it is a reversal, and 'being confined to' is the insertion, so the surface's sickbed is only a small bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both describe someone crooked who takes bribes or cheats.

clue.text: Make one slip translating this letter from abroad

indicators.note: translating means changing from one form to another, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone makes a single mistake putting foreign correspondence into English.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'letter' is a character of an alphabet, not a piece of post. 'Make' links to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Every single run I must grab quickly

parts.note: all means every single one

indicators.note: must grab means the word for I takes the run inside itself

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A batsman knows he has to take each run without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must grab' puts R inside EGO, the psychologist's word for 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian musical direction to play at a brisk tempo.

clue.text: Drier caparisons

definitions.meaning: a folding frame on which washing is hung to air indoors
as a verb, to caparison is to dress a steed in ornamental coverings; read the two parts as verb and object

explanation.definitionFit: It is a frame for airing laundry, and split in two it whimsically says what someone decking out a steed does.
